sections.h2: Who bills and who values property in Worth County
sections.html:
Worth County runs billing and valuation through different offices. The assessors alone set what a parcel is worth. The elected tax commissioner, who answers to neither the assessors nor the county commissioners, mails the statements. A seller needs the payoff from one and the value history from the other.

For pricing context, the county had an estimated 20,059 people in July 2025, with a median home value of $104,900 and owners in 73.7% of houses. Rent runs a median $864, so a landlord buying the house would be pricing against that figure.

On sales, Georgia's rule is short: the January 1 owner owes the year, and a March or June closing returns nothing. Build the closing statement with that in mind.

Call the tax commissioner for bills and payoffs, and call the assessors for values, returns and exemptions.

You can pay online, mail a check to the Room 15 address, phone in a payment, or use the drop box in the alley between the courthouse and the jail.

sections.h2: When the Worth County bill is due
sections.html:
Land, buildings and business property are paid in two parts, one due October 15 and the other November 15. Manufactured homes follow an April 1 date instead. A weekend deadline rolls to Monday.

Schedules can move with the digest, so treat the date on your own statement as final and phone the office if a closing lands near a deadline.

Georgia's default is December 20 unless a local government moves it, with interest held off until 60 days past the bill's postmark. Request the exact late charges along with your payoff, and ask whether the bill for your parcel has already gone out.

  • Only a USPS-dated postmark proves a payment was on time. A meter stamp is rejected.
  • The office takes installments of any size, yet charges keep growing on the unpaid remainder.
  • Statements go to the homeowner and never to the lender. Mortgage companies receive a data file, so forward your bill if escrow pays it.

sections.h2: Solid waste fee on the tax bill
sections.html:
Any residential or business structure outside the cities carries an annual $264.00 solid waste fee, added to the same bill. The Board of Commissioners adopted it by resolution beginning in 2019.

Two relief paths exist. If a structure is dilapidated or vacant for the entire year, the owner can file a waiver request for the Board of Commissioners to approve. Owners over 65 whose total household income is $15,200 or less can qualify for an elderly exemption by completing an affidavit at the commissioners' office, reachable at (229) 776-8200, extension 1.

An inherited or empty rural house may carry the fee even when nobody has lived there. Ask whether a waiver was ever filed, and include any unpaid fee in the payoff figure.

sections.h2: How to contest a Worth County value
sections.html:
Your written appeal must reach the assessors within 45 days of the date printed on the notice. State the grounds (taxability, value, uniformity, or a refused exemption) and name the route you want.

Before April 1 each year, owners may file a return stating a preferred value. The assessors review it and, if they disagree, mail a notice carrying their figure, which starts the clock. Questions about the form go to (229) 776-8203.

The three routes are the equalization board, a hearing officer, or an arbitrator. State revenue staff oversee the process but cannot reverse a single parcel's outcome. Any refund from a final value is processed automatically.

Gather recent sales of similar houses, photographs of defects and any repair estimates before you file, and keep a copy of the written appeal along with proof of the mailing date.

Homestead status requires owning and occupying the house on New Year's Day, and the assessors' office approves each application. Forms can arrive in any month, though April 1 is the last day that helps the current bill.

Approval rolls forward each year while you stay put. A move or a deed change restarts the process, so a buyer files fresh after closing.

Other programs worth asking about:

  • The freeport exemption for business personal property, handled by the assessors.
  • Special assessment programs, which the assessors can describe by phone.
  • The elderly exemption from the solid waste fee described above.

A 30-day warning letter goes out before any lien is filed. The lien, a FiFa, lands on the General Execution Docket held by the superior court clerk once a balance passes 90 days late, and because the entry is public, credit bureaus may pick it up.

Full payment of tax, fees, penalties and interest cancels it. Liens are not sold over the counter here. Once a levy and tax sale advertisement begin, the office urges walking the payment in.

Manufactured and modular homes count as personal property, and the location permit is withheld until the current mobile home tax is paid in full. A seller with one on the lot should settle that account first.

sections.h2: What a seller does before closing
sections.html:
Begin with a call to the tax commissioner for the payoff and the current late charges. Then ask the assessors whether your homestead is on file and what value is on your assessment notice. If the house sits outside a city, ask the commissioners' office about the solid waste fee and any waiver. Order a copy of your warranty deed from the Clerk of Courts if you do not have one handy. At the closing table, the payoff comes out of your proceeds and the year's tax is split in the contract, because the county bills one owner and never divides a year. A cash buyer purchasing as-is skips repair talks, but these tax steps stay the same, so finishing them early keeps the sale from stalling.

Two small habits help. Keep the postmarked envelope or the receipt from every payment, because the postmark is the only proof the office accepts. And if your mortgage company pays from escrow, forward any statement that reaches you, since the lender gets a data file rather than the printed bill. Sellers with a mobile home on the property should also confirm that the current mobile home tax is paid and the location permit is in hand before a buyer walks the lot.

faqs.q: Where is the Worth County tax office?
faqs.a: At 201 N. Main St., Room 15 in Sylvester, or by phone at (229) 776-8204. You can also pay online, through the mail, or at the drop box in the alley beside the jail.

faqs.q: What are the Worth County tax due dates?
faqs.a: October 15 and November 15 for land and buildings, and April 1 for mobile homes. Your bill has the final word.

faqs.q: What is the cutoff to dispute a Worth County value?
faqs.a: Forty-five days, counting from the notice. Call the assessors at (229) 776-8203 for the form.

faqs.q: Does the solid waste fee apply to a vacant house?
faqs.a: It can, though a structure dilapidated or empty all year may earn a waiver. The commissioners' office at (229) 776-8200, extension 1 decides.

faqs.q: Will a late payment hurt my credit?
faqs.a: Only if a lien is recorded, which can follow a balance more than 90 days late. The tax office itself reports nothing to credit bureaus.
